name: Build the Rota
description: Business Ladder, Operations, Level 3 (Run a workflow). A week’s rota for a pub, a care home or a warehouse: 5 to 12 staff with contracted hours, pay rates, skills (keyholder, personal licence, medication, first aid, forklift), availability and leave, 11 hours’ rest between shifts (12 for under-18s, counting last week’s last shift), a 48-hour cap, under-18 limits, exact cover per shift, a weekend fairness rule and a late message. The rota is checked rule by rule and its wage cost compared with the cheapest legal rota an exact branch-and-bound search can prove.
hook: Cover every shift, break no working-time rule, and spend the least on wages.
author: Gauntlet Real-World Pack

cases.prompt:
From: Callum Reid
Subject: Rota for the week of Mon 2 Nov 2026

Hi, can you build next week’s rota for The Fox & Fiddle in Shrewsbury? It has to keep every rule below, and I want it as cheap as possible on wages.

SHIFTS
- Open (O): 10:00–17:30, 7 paid hours (the rest is an unpaid break).
- Close (C): 17:30–01:00 (finishes the next morning), 7 paid hours (the rest is an unpaid break).

COVER (exactly this many people on each shift: no more, no fewer)
Shift | Mon | Tue | Wed | Thu | Fri | Sat | Sun
Open | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 2
Close | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 3 | 2
Every Open shift needs at least 1 keyholder on it.
Every Close shift needs at least 1 keyholder and 1 personal licence holder on it.

STAFF (pay is per paid hour; contracted hours are the least and most each person must be given this week)
Name | Role | Pay | Contracted hours | Skills | Availability
Callum Reid | Manager | £15.20 | 26–48 | keyholder, personal licence holder | any shift
Nadia Hussain | Deputy manager | £13.90 | 20–40 | keyholder, personal licence holder | any shift
Tomasz Wójcik | Bar staff | £12.71 | 14–40 | keyholder | not Tuesdays
Ines Carvalho | Bar staff | £12.71 | 0–28 | - | evenings only
Rhys Morgan | Bar staff | £10.85 | 0–28 | - | on holiday Mon–Wed
Hamza Ali | Bar staff | £12.71 | 0–21 | - | any shift

RULES FOR THIS ROTA
1. At least 11 hours’ rest between the end of one shift and the start of the next (12 hours for anyone under 18). This includes the last shift someone worked last week.
2. Nobody works more than 48 paid hours in the week (use this as a strict weekly cap for this exercise; no opt-outs).
3. Under-18s: no work at all between 22:00 and 06:00, no more than 8 paid hours in a day and 40 in the week.
4. Everyone gets between the least and the most of their contracted hours.
5. Weekend fairness: a weekend shift is any shift that starts on a Saturday or Sunday. Among the staff who are available for at least one weekend shift (bank staff excepted), the number of weekend shifts each person works must be within one of each other (the most minus the least is 0 or 1).
6. Nobody works a shift they are not available for, and nobody works two shifts at once.
7. Wage cost = paid hours × (hourly pay + any shift premium), added up over every shift worked. Make it as low as possible.

Answer with the rota as the people on every shift (shift codes are the day and the shift letter, e.g. "Mon-O"; first names are fine) and the total wage cost in pounds, in this JSON format:
```json
{"rota": {"Mon-O": ["<name>"]}, "total": 0.00}
```
Give exactly one answer as a single JSON block. Do not offer alternatives: a reply that contains two different answers, or a value that says "or", is marked wrong. You may explain your working before the JSON.
cases.notes: [easy] pub, 6 staff, 14 shifts, 24 slots. Cheapest legal rota £2,194.57 (exact branch-and-bound, 101 nodes).
